description.narrative: After a period of inactivity, the Tripartite Commission on Reporting under Ratified International Labour Standards has set itself a work plan, with a first meeting held in 2022 and another scheduled for 2023. This mechanism, under which the tripartite constituents meet effectively to plan and carry out standard-related issues as listed in Article 5 of Convention No. 144, has been strengthened through more frequent tripartite consultations. Issues discussed by the Committee in 2022 and those scheduled for discussion in 2023 concern(ed) not only reporting under ratified Conventions (article 22 reports) and article 19 General Survey reports, but also a number of other related issues, such as the reform of the national labour legislation and the ratification of Conventions. ILO assistance included the organization of the meeting of the Tripartite Workshop on Reporting in August 2022, which was instrumental in the revitalization of tripartite dialogue on standards-related issues, such as labour law reform and application in practice of International Labour Standards. A similar meeting is planned for August 2023 with financial and technical assistance from the ILO.

description.narrative: In 2022, all article 22 reports requested on ratified Conventions (C29, C105, C87, C98, C100, C111, MLC) were submitted for their consideration by the CEACR. They are the main source of information (together with any observations received from employers’ and workers’ organizations) for the CEACR when considering the implementation in law and practice of ratified Conventions . All reports were received before the deadline of September 1, 2022. These reports, which were of a very high quality and responded to all requests made by the CEACR, , are essential to enable the CEACR to conduct its work in a timely manner and adopt relevant comments during its session in November/December.. The timely submission of these reports fills a gap compared with previous years, as there was an important backlog of reports not received under ratified conventions having caused issues of carrying out the supervision of ratified Conventions by the Gambia in the past. . By way of illustration, no reports were received between 2013 and 2018. However, a timid recovery was noted in 2019, before falling back into a shortage of reports for the years 2020 and 2021. Furthermore, in 2023, the reports due under Conventions C100 and C111 were again received by the CEACR before the deadline of September 1, 2023. In 2022, the ILO mobilized technical expertise to help the Government collect the relevant information to be included in all reports under ratified Conventions. This included in-depth discussions with various Government officials and technical entities on information to be included in the reports under ratified Conventions in relation to child labor, forced labor, freedom of association and working conditions for workers in the maritime sector. The ILO support also included the organization of a workshop, in August 2022, with the National Reporting Commission, which included presentations of the relevant Conventions, outstanding requests made by the CEACR, and discussions between participants on the level of implementation of Conventions for which reports were due, as well as on the inclusion of relevant information. In view of the recent ratification of the MLC 2006 and the country's reporting obligations in 2022 (first report), two Government officials also participated in the online training course on MLC 2006 reporting in 2021, which assisted in the preparation of the report in 2022 on the implementation of this Convention. In addition, in 2023, the Standards Specialist prepared a table listing the outstanding requests made by the CEACR (together with some explanations and examples) to facilitate the drafting of the report on the application of Conventions Nos. 100 and 111. In addition, thanks to the capacity-building of a national expert working with the Government on reporting, the ILO can now count on expertise in the field of International Labour Standards for future relevant assignments.
